title: litkb Codex review report
description: The fixed shape of the Codex review stage's output (docs/SCHEMAS.md). One row per CITATION OCCURRENCE of the review under test, numbered 1-based in document order, plus editorial findings that are not citation defects. Produced by Codex under `codex exec --output-schema`, validated and hash-stamped by qc/instruments/litkb_codex_review.py, graded by qc/instruments/litkb_acceptance.py codex.

review_sha256.description: sha256 of the review file's RAW BYTES. The wrapper overwrites whatever the model wrote here, so the report can never disagree with the file it was produced from.

context_sha256.description: sha256 of the context file's RAW BYTES, stamped by the wrapper for the same reason.

citations.description: One entry per citation OCCURRENCE, not per distinct block: the run-2 review carried 13 occurrences over 6 blocks, and collapsing them would make `n` mean nothing.

n.description: 1-based index of this citation in document order, as review_check.citations() enumerates them.

block_id.description: The block uuid the citation names, copied from the citation token.

quote_head.description: The first <=80 characters of the quote, so a reader can see which span was graded without the report carrying the paper.

verdict.description: SUPPORTED: the sentence asserts no more than the quote, read with its whole block, supports. OVERREACH: the quote supports something, and the sentence asserts more (added magnitude, causation, comparison, or a supplied antecedent). UNSUPPORTED: the quote does not support the sentence at all.

reason.description: Why, in one or two sentences. Naming the added element for an OVERREACH.

editorial.description: Findings that are not per-citation: section titles, Scope, incomplete disclosure. May be empty, and an empty array is a statement, not an omission.

where.description: Where in the review: a section heading, a line, or `Scope`.

session_id.description: The Codex session/thread id, stamped by the wrapper from the --json event stream so a follow-up can resume the same worker. Absent when the stream carried none.

session_id_key.description: Which key of the --json stream the session id was read from. Wrapper-stamped, and recorded because the event shape is not documented in `codex exec --help`.
